obligations.note: The new `fx_rate` makes an outbound call to `FX_RATES_URL = "http://fx.fernbrook.example/rates"`, which is plain http rather than https. It calls `outbound._transport.send` directly, bypassing the integrations list, so the exhaustive TLS control test over `integrations.py` cannot see this endpoint.

The treasury FX service is a new outbound integration. It is not listed in `controls/payments/asset-inventory.json`, which has only core-banking, sanctions-screening and statement-delivery, so it has no owner or data classification.
The exception register has no entry for ENC-2 or INV-1 on `payments.payments` or `payments.integrations`. The deviations are therefore not covered by any approved, unexpired exception.

`required_approvals`, `is_fully_approved` and `DUAL_CONTROL_THRESHOLD` are unchanged by the diff. The exhaustive proof in ACR-0401 still applies, and the dual-control grid control test is listed as passing.

`approve` and `is_fully_approved` are unchanged, and the exhaustive maker-checker control test is listed as passing. However, that pass comes from a JUnit report whose provenance does not match the CI run (see CHG-4), and there is no ledger entry to fall back on.
`release` is unchanged, but the only evidence is sample-level: a single-run trace (ACR-0403) and a sample control test. The obligation requires exhaustive evidence.
The ledger entries covering `payments.py` (`required_approvals` in ACR-0401 and `release` in ACR-0403) cover code the diff does not alter, so that evidence has not lapsed.

Ticket CHG-25066 is a standard ticket approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-04, before the change was opened. Its component `payments.payments` covers the only touched file, `payments.py`.
Sofia Santos approved the code review. She holds `change_approver` for payments and is not the author, Linh Nguyen.
The code_review approval names head commit bfec8e07, which is the only commit on the change.

`run.json` claims a success on head from ci-runner-06 starting 2026-10-06. The attached JUnit report, however, is timestamped 2026-10-23 (after the 2026-10-12 review time) on host `dev-laptop-7.local`, so it is not credibly this run's output. The new `fx_rate` code also has no tests.

summary: PR-1924 adds a direct outbound call to an FX service over plain http. It bypasses the integrations registry and the endpoint is missing from the asset inventory. This violates ENC-2 and INV-1, and no approved exception covers either deviation. In addition, the CI test report's timestamp and host do not match the recorded CI run, so the testing evidence is unreliable. The change is rejected.
